OBJECTIVES
The Vanderbilt Chemistry Department strives to ensure that our
international applicants understand the application process for
our Ph.D. program. We recognize that international students
face specific challenges when applying to US institutions and
our goal is to provide transparent and beneficial information for
submitting a strong application.

GRADUATE STUDENT SUPPORT
The graduate program in chemistry provides year-round
financial support, guaranteed for five full years to all full-time
graduate students in good standing. The financial support
package includes tuition, health insurance, and a competitive
stipend that helps cover living expenses.

APPLICATION FAQS
APPLICATION PROCESS
Deadlines
Applications traditionally open on August 1 each year. Our priority deadline is December 1, 2026. The FINAL
application deadline is December 15, 2026, after which point no applications will be accepted.
Materials
Transcripts: Unofficial transcripts are perfectly acceptable for the application stage.
GRE: The General GRE is not required but is encouraged.
Recommender Contact Information: You will be asked for official email addresses and titles of all
recommenders.
English Proficiency: Most students will complete either the TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo. Some students may
be eligible for a language examination waiver. The Graduate School minimums are listed below:
TOEFL: 89
IELTS: 7
Duolingo: 130
Statement of Purpose
Letters of Recommendation
Letters should come from a research advisor, a professor who can judge your intellectual and laboratory
preparation for graduate courses and research in chemistry or a supervisor (work or volunteer opportunities).
We require a minimum of 3 letters and a maximum of 5. You may submit your application prior to our receipt of
all your supporting letters. However, your application will not be reviewed until the required three letters are
received.
WRITING A STATEMENT OF PURPOSE
We often get questions about the Statement of Purpose requirement within our application. This statement serves to
highlight your accomplishments, previous research, and future research goals and/or endeavors. We do not have a
specific word count or length requirement; However, we encourage applicants to aim for about 2 pages. Below is
what we hope to see our applicants highlight:
Tell us about your academic journey
Tell us why you want to go to graduate school and what you expect to accomplish here
Specify who you would like to work with at Vanderbilt
TYPICAL OUTLINE OF A STATEMENT OF PURPOSE
1. Introduce yourself and your motivation for graduate school
We want to know who you are! Explain what has shaped your decision to apply to graduate school. This
introduction should be concise. (1-2 paragraphs)
2. Summarize your undergraduate and/or previous graduate career
Highlight research experiences. Explain who you’ve worked with, what the project was, your role, and if there
were results and/or outcomes.
Highlight your experiences beyond your curricular requirements. This could be a paper, poster or thesis you
worked on.
Highlight your work experiences relevant to chemistry. This should only include work that relates to the field
of chemistry and may include internships.

3. Explain any current activities relevant to chemistry
If you took a gap year or are applying to graduate school not directly out of undergraduate studies, tell us
what you are currently doing.
4. Tell us what you want to do in the future
What area of chemistry are you most interested in? Who would you like to work with at Vanderbilt? What are
your future career goals.
GENERAL FAQS
We’ve compiled a list of general FAQs that we receive from international applicants for your review:
Q: Do I need to secure an advisor prior to applying?
A: No! At Vanderbilt, we do not admit students for specific labs. Rather, our admitted students complete three
lab rotations in their first semester to find their research lab. We encourage all applicants to familiarize
themselves with the faculty and research conducted at VU Chemistry. The faculty you specify in your statement
could be the laboratories in which you complete your rotations.
Q: Do I need to email someone to ask for an application fee waiver?
A: The Chemistry Department does not offer discretionary application fee waivers. The Graduate School does
provide application fee waivers for students who meet their requirements. Learn more about the application fee
waivers available through the Graduate School.
Q: How will I be notified if I am admitted to the program?
A: All official admission decisions will be released to the application portal. You do not need to email the
department for a decision. All applications will receive an official decision.
Q: When should I expect to be notified about my admittance decision?
A: Typically, we strive to make all admission decisions by mid-January of each year.
Q: Do I have to apply for TA or RA positions to secure my funding?
A: No! All of our students will be funded based on departmental and/or PI needs. Most students will TA for 4
semesters.
Q: Do you accept applications for the spring or summer semesters?
A: No! All of our applicants should apply for the fall semester.
